description: A/B test of the identification-v1 prompt rewrite against the current production prompt, across two monitor threads (16 subtrees: 12 from thread 736b1b30 + 4 from thread 0dfc0e00). The rewrite mirrors the extraction-v1 buyer-utility shift: the abstract 3-condition gate is replaced with a BUYER-RELEVANT TEST (verdicts incl. informal, named-attribute observations, comparisons, reasoned prospective-buyer concerns, reliability/issue claims, reference-tier informational claims) plus an ALWAYS RETURN [] list (jokes, pure questions, bare logistics, settings dumps, intent-to-test, generic brand/panel-tech statements, hypothetical-product chatter). Same-author anaphor chains are promoted to a top priority with a worked example. Verbatim model preservation is its own section with concrete contrasts (G8sd, 34GS9QE, MPG341 stay verbatim). Off-cheat-sheet products are explicitly emittable. Goals: (a) deepseek-v4-flash with v1 closes the gap to gpt-5.4-mini judge scores; (b) cost per run within ~10% of current; (c) no regression on schema validity, no model-string fabrication. The hand-curated golden encodes the recall bar — keyed by subtreeId, shared with the v4-flash-vs-gpt-mini scenario.

goldenOutput.note: Hand-curated Opus reference. Keyed by subtreeId — find the entry matching the current subtree's id. Treat as a quality floor: candidate must match or exceed this recall, with no more false positives and no fabricated model strings (verbatim '34GS9QE' must stay '34GS9QE').
Same golden file (keyed by subtreeId). The Samsung subtrees stress-test verbatim variant preservation — 'G8sd', 'SD', 'SB' must NOT be silently upgraded to 'S34DG850SU'.

expectations.desiredOutcome: The candidate must surface EVERY buyer-relevant product reference — the same standard the extraction step applies to quotes. Buyer-relevant means: a future buyer would learn something from knowing this comment is about this product. That includes owner verdicts (even informal: 'all I can say is wow', 'absolutely insane'), reasoned prospective-buyer concerns ('biggest concern is G-sync', 'feeling like a huge gamble'), reference-tier informational claims ('TFT says it's the MSI', 'firmware update fixes the HDR'), comparisons ('better panel at a lower price'), issue reports, anti-recommendations with reason, and reliability claims. Schema-valid JSON conforming to subtree-identification.schema for every subtree. Every PLAN comment has an entry even when products is empty. Anaphoric and pronominal references resolve to brand+model when the surrounding subtree makes the referent unambiguous, including same-author earlier [PLAN] nodes (not only direct [CONTEXT] parents). Verbatim model preservation: '34GS9QE' is NOT silently upgraded to '34GS95QE-B', 'G8sd' is NOT upgraded to 'S34DG850SU', 'MPG341' is NOT upgraded to 'MPG 341CQPX'. Variant differentiation: 175 Hz MAG 341CQP is NOT collapsed into 240 Hz MPG 341CQPX. Off-cheat-sheet products that the commenter explicitly names AND evaluates (e.g. owner mentioning 'LG 34GN850' or '45GX950A') are emitted with the commenter's text plus a searchKeyword. contentQuality is calibrated: 'high' = substantive evaluation with specifics, comparison, or detailed first-hand experience; 'medium' = verdict or preference without depth ('it's great', 'absolutely insane', 'solid'); 'low' = product named but not evaluated (bare ownership, listing, availability question, anti-recommendation with no reason). When borderline, pick the lower level. Generic brand or panel-tech statements ('OLED panels in general', 'qdoled >> woled', 'Don't get LG') do NOT produce product entries.

judge.instructions: Score each candidate on three dimensions, each 1-10. The goal is buyer-utility: every comment a future buyer would want attributed to a product must be captured — missing a real reference loses downstream extraction signal; hallucinating a product corrupts ratings. Fabricating model strings (emitting '34GS95QE-B' when the commenter wrote '34GS9QE', or 'S34DG850SU' when the commenter wrote 'G8sd') drops faithfulness to ≤3 regardless of recall. (1) faithfulness (weight: highest) — every buyer-relevant product reference is surfaced, including: anaphoric and pronominal references ('both are solid', 'the LG', 'this monitor'); same-author chains via earlier [PLAN] nodes (not only direct [CONTEXT] parents); informal owner endorsements ('all I can say is wow', 'absolutely insane'); reasoned prospective-buyer concerns ('biggest concern is G-sync', 'feeling like a huge gamble'); reference-tier informational claims ('TFT says it's the MSI', 'firmware update fixes the HDR'); reliability/issue claims; anti-recommendations with reason. Verbatim model preservation is part of faithfulness. No products hallucinated from generic brand or panel-tech statements. (2) calibration (weight: medium) — contentQuality matches depth per the schema enum: 'high' = substantive with specifics, comparison, or detailed first-hand experience; 'medium' = verdict or preference without depth; 'low' = named but not evaluated. Borderline cases err lower. Variant accuracy (MAG 341CQP at 175 Hz vs MPG 341CQPX at 240 Hz; G85SD vs S34DG850SU) also counts here. (3) completeness (weight: low) — every PLAN comment has an entry even when products is empty; jokes/thanks/meta-replies produce empty arrays without inventing products. Use the goldenOutput as a quality floor: candidates should match or exceed its recall with no more false positives. Return JSON {candidates:[{candidateId, scores:{faithfulness, calibration, completeness}, rationale}], verdict}. Verdict format: 'best=<id>' | 'tie' | 'none-acceptable'. In the rationale, call out specific subtrees and comment IDs where the candidates diverge from the golden or each other — that is the most actionable signal for prompt iteration.
